message.content:
Below are two ways to spin‑up a **Google Cloud** virtual machine that boots Ubuntu 20.04 LTS and attaches one or more NVIDIA GPUs.  
(If you truly need an *RTX A6000* – that specific card isn’t offered on GCP at present – replace `GPU_TYPE` with whatever GPU family you actually want.)

---

### 1️⃣  Using the `gcloud` Command Line Tool  

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

PROJECT_ID="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
ZONE="us-central1-b"          # pick your preferred zone
INSTANCE_NAME="my-gpu-instance"

# Pick a machine type that fits your workload:
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-highcpu-32"   # change as needed

# Choose a GPU family & count
ACCELERATOR_COUNT=1            # how many cards?
ACCELERATOR_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a100"   # <-- substitute here

# Create the instance
gcloud beta compute \
    instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
        --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
        --zone="$ZONE" \
        --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
        --boot-disk-size=50GB \
        --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
        --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
        --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
        --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \      # optional init script
        --accelerators=count=$ACCELERATOR_COUNT,type=$ACCELERATOR_TYPE \
        --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
        --reservation-affinity=any
```

#### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--project`, `--zone` | Target GCP project / location |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM profile |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root volume |
| `--image-family`, `--image-project` | Boot from official Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--scopes` | Grant full Cloud‑Platform scope so drivers install automatically |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script=` | Optional shell script run after first boot |
| `--accelerators` | Attach GPU(s); adjust `count` & `type` |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | Keep the instance running during maintenance windows |

> ⚠️ **Important:** Before launching, make sure the “Compute Engine” APIs are enabled in your project and that you’ve authorized the `gcloud` tool (`gcloud auth login`).  

---

### 2️⃣  Directly via the REST API (Insert Method)

Use the following JSON body against the endpoint:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json
Cache-Control: no-cache

{
  "name": "{INSTANCE_NAME}",
  "description": "Ubuntu 20.04 + GPU",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-highcpu-32",

  "disks": [
    {
      "deviceName": "bootdisk",
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 50
      }
    }
  ],

  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "accessConfigs": [{ "type":"ONE_TO_ONE_NAT","name":"External NAT"}],
      "subnetworks": ["global/networks/default"]
    }
  ],

  "serviceAccounts": [{
     "email":"default",
     "scopes":["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
  }],

  "guestAccelerators":[
    {
       "acceleratorCount":1,
       "acceleratorType":"projects/{PROJECT_ID}/regions/us-central1/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ]
}
```

Replace `{}` placeholders with actual values:

| Placeholder | Example Value |
|-------------|---------------|
| `{PROJECT_ID}` | `my-awesome-proj` |
| `{ZONE}` | `us-central1-b` |
| `{INSTANCE_NAME}` | `my-gpu-instance` |
| `{ACCESS_TOKEN}` | OAuth token obtained via `gcloud auth print-access-token` |

After sending the POST request, monitor the returned Operation resource until its status becomes `"DONE"`—that’s when the instance is ready.

---

### Quick Checklist

1. **Billing Enabled** – Ensure the target project has active billing.  
2. **API Access** – Enable the Compute Engine API (`services.enable`) in the console or via `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`.  
3. **Quota** – Verify you’re under quota limits for CPUs, disks, and GPUs in the selected zone.  
4. **Driver Installation** – By granting the `cloud-platform` scope, the system will auto‑install NVIDIA driver packages upon first boot. No extra steps required unless you prefer custom versions.  

Happy computing! 🚀
